128327.e: With premium services using short numbers, extra costs are added to your phone bill. This quickly adds up.

128328.q: What does a block on premium services from your mobile provider do?
a: Expensive extra services cannot be charged
You can no longer make calls
128328.e: With a block like this, no paid extra services can be charged to your phone bill. This protects you from nasty surprises.
128328.m: A block protects you from hidden costs.

128329.q: With many contracts, what happens when the included data allowance is used up?
a: The internet gets slower or it costs extra
The phone switches off for ever
The contract is extended for free
128329.e: Depending on the contract, the speed is reduced or extra data is charged. That is why it is worth keeping an eye on how much you use.
128329.m: Keep an eye on your data allowance.

128330.q: Which question should you ask yourself before every new subscription?
a: Do I really need this regularly?
Do all my friends have it?
128330.e: A subscription is only worth it if you use it often. Otherwise it is cheaper to pay separately only when you need it.
128330.m: Only subscribe to what you use often.

128331.q: How can you recognise a secure connection in an online shop?
a: The address starts with https and shows a padlock
The shop has lots of colourful pictures
128331.e: The “https” and the padlock show that the data is sent in encrypted form. But that alone does not guarantee that the shop is trustworthy.

128332.q: What is a typical sign of a fake shop?
a: Extremely low prices and no legal notice
A clear legal notice with an address
128332.e: Fraudulent shops lure people with unrealistically low prices. Contact details are often missing, and you are asked to pay in advance.
128332.m: Too cheap to be true? Be careful!

128333.q: Why is paying in advance risky with an unknown online shop?
a: You pay before you have the goods
You pay less in the end
128333.e: If you pay in advance, the money is gone before the goods arrive. If nothing comes, it is hard to get your money back.
128333.m: Do not pay unknown sellers in advance.

128334.q: What is the general rule for online purchases in Switzerland?
a: There is no general legal right to cancel
You can return anything within 30 days
128334.e: Unlike in the EU, Switzerland has no general right to cancel online purchases. Whether you can return things is set out in the shop's terms and conditions.
128334.m: Returns? Read the terms and conditions.

128335.q: What can you find in an online shop's terms and conditions?
a: The rules on delivery, payment and returns
128335.e: The general terms and conditions set the rules for the purchase. For example, they say whether you may send goods back and who pays the costs.
128335.m: Terms and conditions are the shop's rules of the game.

128336.q: A T-shirt costs 15 francs online plus 8 francs delivery. In the shop it costs 20 francs. Which is cheaper?
128336.e: Online it costs 23 francs with delivery, in the shop only 20 francs. Always add delivery costs when you compare.
128336.m: Delivery costs are part of the price.

128337.q: Why can an order from abroad end up more expensive than expected?
a: VAT and customs fees may be added
Because you have to order twice
128337.e: For parcels from abroad, customs charge Swiss VAT depending on the value, and the delivery company often adds a fee.
128337.m: Ordering from abroad: think about customs and fees.

128338.q: You get a message: “Your parcel is waiting, pay 2 francs using this link.” What do you do?
a: Do not click and delete the message
Enter your card details straight away
Send the link to all your friends
128338.e: Messages like this are often phishing. Scammers use them to get card or account details. You check real delivery companies on their official website.

128339.q: Which statement about online reviews is true?
a: Some reviews are bought or fake
Reviews are always written by the state
128339.e: There are fake reviews that make a product look better. Look for lots of different, detailed opinions.

128340.q: What does “pay by invoice” mean when shopping online?
a: You get the goods first and pay afterwards
128340.e: When you pay by invoice, you only pay after delivery. But you must keep to the payment deadline, otherwise reminder fees are added.
128340.m: Paying by invoice: pay later, but on time.

128341.q: Why should you not save your payment details in every online shop?
a: Because they can be misused after a data leak
Because shopping then gets more expensive
Because otherwise the phone gets slow
128341.e: Saved payment details make shopping convenient, but they also make spontaneous purchases easier. In a hacker attack they can be stolen.

128342.q: Why do people often spend more online than in a shop?
a: You do not see the money and can order at any time
Because everything is more expensive online
Because you cannot see prices online
128342.e: A click is quick, and paying feels less real than with cash. On top of that, shops keep suggesting more products.

128343.q: A phone costs 600 francs in cash or 12 instalments of 55 francs. How much more does buying in instalments cost?
128343.e: 12 times 55 makes 660 francs. That is 60 francs more than paying in cash. Instalments often cost extra.
128343.m: Instalments usually make things more expensive.

128344.q: What is the interest on a loan?
a: The price you pay for the borrowed money
128344.e: If you borrow money, you have to pay back more than you received. The extra amount is the interest, the price of the loan.

128345.q: What does “Buy now, pay later” mean in online shops?
a: You pay later, but must pay on time
The goods are free for ever
128345.e: You get the goods straight away and pay later or in instalments. If you miss the deadline, you have to pay reminder fees or interest. This tempts people into buying things they cannot afford.

128346.q: Why is a small loan for a new games console usually not a good idea?
a: You pay interest for something you do not urgently need
Because you never have to pay the loan back
128346.e: A loan makes the purchase more expensive because of the interest. For things you want, it is wiser to save first.
128346.m: Save for wants, do not borrow.

128347.q: Which statement about paying in instalments is true?
a: Several instalments at once can wreck your budget
You only have to pay instalments if you feel like it
128347.e: Every instalment is a fixed cost for many months. If you have several, you quickly lose track and have little money free.
128347.m: Many instalments, little room to manoeuvre.

128348.q: With leasing, what does not belong to you during the contract period?
128348.e: With leasing you pay monthly to use something, but the product still belongs to the leasing company. At the end you usually have to give it back.

a: A notice that a bill is still unpaid
128349.e: If you do not pay a bill on time, you get a reminder. Often extra reminder fees are added.
128349.m: Paying on time saves reminder fees.

128350.q: How do people often fall into a debt trap?
a: They take on new debts to pay off old ones
128350.e: If you pay off old debts with newly borrowed money, you end up with even more debt. On top of that come interest and fees.
128350.m: Paying debts with debts makes it worse.

128351.q: What is the first sensible step when you notice that your money is not enough?
a: Get an overview of all your spending and debts
128351.e: If you know how much you owe and to whom, you can make a plan. If there are problems, parents or a debt advice service can help.
128351.m: Face it instead of looking away.

128352.q: Max owes three friends 20 francs each. He gets 30 francs pocket money. What is sensible?
a: Agree a repayment plan with his friends
Borrow money from a fourth friend
128352.e: Max owes 60 francs, more than his pocket money. With a plan he can pay back the debts step by step.
128352.m: Talk honestly and make a plan.

128353.q: What is a warning sign that someone is spending too much?
a: The money is regularly gone before the end of the month
You have saved something every month
128353.e: If the money always runs out before the next payday, spending is too high. Then a budget is worth it.
128353.m: If money runs out before the end of the month, check your budget.

128354.q: What happens if you overdraw your bank account, if the bank allows it?
a: You owe the bank money and pay interest
The bank gives you the money
128354.e: If you spend more money than is in your account, you are borrowing it from the bank. The bank usually charges high interest for this.
128354.m: Being in the red costs money.

128355.q: All your friends have the expensive new shoes. What helps against pressure to buy?
a: Thinking about whether you really want them yourself
Taking out a loan straight away
Forcing your parents to buy them
128355.e: Peer pressure can lead to purchases you cannot afford. If you ask yourself what you really want, you decide more freely.
128355.m: Buy what you want, not what others have.

128356.q: Why do influencers often show particular products in their videos?
a: Because companies pay them or give them presents
Because the products are always the best
128356.e: Many influencers earn money by showing products. That is why their opinion is not always neutral.
128356.m: Influencers often earn money from their tips.

128357.q: What does the label “advert” or “ad” on a post mean?
a: The post was paid for by a company
The post is from the school
128357.e: Paid posts must be recognisable as advertising. That way viewers know that a company is behind it.
128357.m: “Advert” means: something is being sold here.

128358.q: An influencer shares a discount code. What is usually true?
a: The influencer earns money from every purchase
The code makes the product free
The code works in all shops
128358.e: With discount codes or special links, the company can see who led to the purchase. The influencer often gets a commission for it.
128358.m: Discount codes earn the influencer money too.

128359.q: A shop shows: “Only 2 left! Offer ends in 10 minutes.” What is this meant to do?
a: Make you buy quickly without thinking for long
128359.e: Messages like this create time pressure. You are meant to buy at once instead of thinking about whether you need the product.
128359.m: Time pressure is an advertising trick.

128360.q: Why do you often see adverts online for things you searched for recently?
a: Because your browsing behaviour is analysed
128360.e: Websites and apps collect data about your searches and clicks. They use it to show you targeted adverts meant to get you to buy.

128361.q: Which question helps you look at advertising critically?
a: Who earns money if I buy this?
Is the music in the advert cool?
128361.e: If you ask who profits from the purchase, you recognise the purpose behind the advert. That way you are less easily influenced.
128361.m: Always ask: who earns money from this?

128362.q: What does the price per kilo or per litre on the price label show?
a: How much a set amount costs, for comparing
128362.e: With the unit price you can compare packs of different sizes. That way you can see which offer is really cheaper.
128362.m: The price per kilo shows the better deal.

128363.q: Pack A: 500 g for 4 francs. Pack B: 1 kg for 7 francs. Which is cheaper per kilo?
128363.e: Pack A costs 8 francs per kilo, pack B only 7 francs. The larger pack is cheaper here, but only if you need all of it.
128363.m: Always convert to the same measure.

128364.q: A jumper costs 40 francs. There is a 25% discount. How much do you pay?
128364.e: 25% of 40 francs is 10 francs. 40 minus 10 makes 30 francs.

128365.q: Special offer: “3 for 2”. What does that mean?
a: You take 3 and only pay for 2
128365.e: With “3 for 2”, one item is free. But it is only worth it if you really need all three.
128365.m: A special offer is only worth it if you need it.

128366.q: What is often true when comparing branded products with own-brand products?
a: Own brands are often cheaper with similar quality
128366.e: Shops' own brands usually cost less because less is spent on advertising them. The quality is often comparable.

128368.q: In Switzerland, what is the rise in prices often called?
128368.e: When prices rise in general, people in Switzerland speak of “Teuerung”, the rising cost of living. Another word for it is inflation.
128368.m: Teuerung means everything is getting more expensive.

128369.q: A croissant used to cost 1 franc and now costs 1.20 francs. What does this show?
a: You can buy less with the same money
128369.e: When prices rise, you get less for one franc than before. Money loses purchasing power.
128369.m: When prices rise, your money buys less.

128370.q: How is it measured in Switzerland how much prices are rising?
a: With a basket of many typical products
With the price of a single loaf
With the number of cars sold
128370.e: The Federal Statistical Office compares the prices of a basket with many goods and services. This is the national consumer price index.
128370.m: The basket of goods shows the rise in prices.

128371.q: What happens to 100 francs in the piggy bank when prices rise?
a: You can buy less with it later
You can buy more with it
128371.e: The amount stays the same, but things get more expensive. That is why the money in the piggy bank is worth less later.
128371.m: The same money, but you get less for it.

128372.q: What is the opposite of inflation?
a: Discount: a shop has a special offer
128372.e: In deflation, prices fall over a longer time. That sounds good, but it can harm the economy because people put off buying things.

128373.q: What is the job of the Swiss National Bank when it comes to prices?
a: It makes sure prices stay stable
It sets the price of every product
128373.e: The National Bank is meant to ensure price stability. By this it means a rise in prices of less than 2% a year.
128373.m: The National Bank protects the value of the franc.

128377.q: The bike insurance costs 84 francs a year. How much should Luca budget for it each month?
128377.e: 84 francs divided by 12 months makes 7 francs a month.
128377.m: The yearly amount divided by 12 gives the monthly amount.

a: Lots of people pay a little so there is enough for everyone
A game where you win money
A piggy bank just for you
128469.e: With insurance, lots of people regularly pay a small amount. If someone has bad luck, this money is used to help them.
128469.m: Many small payments help the person who needs help.

128470.q: In a class, every child puts one franc into a money box. One child loses their ball. What does the class do?
a: It buys a new ball with the money
It keeps the money for ever
It gives the money to the teacher
128470.e: That is how insurance works: everyone pays in a little. Whoever has bad luck gets help from the shared money box.

128471.q: Why do healthy people also pay into health insurance?
a: Because anyone can get ill one day
Because otherwise they go to prison
Because they get sweets for it
Because healthy people must have more money
128471.e: Nobody knows when they will get ill. That is why everyone pays in, even when they are healthy at the moment. So there is money when it is needed.
128471.m: Healthy today, maybe ill tomorrow: the insurance is there for everyone.

128472.q: Who pays the health insurance for a child?
a: The child with their pocket money
128472.e: Parents take out health insurance for their children and pay for it. In Switzerland children must be insured too.

128473.q: Do babies in Switzerland need health insurance too?
a: Yes, babies must be insured too
Only babies who cry a lot
128473.e: In Switzerland every person who lives here must have basic insurance. That applies to babies too.
128473.m: From baby to grandma: everyone is insured.

128474.q: What is the money called that you pay to the health insurer regularly?
128474.e: The premium is the amount you pay the health insurer regularly. You pay it even when you are healthy.
128474.m: You always pay the premium, ill or healthy.

128475.q: After a visit to the doctor, a letter arrives with an amount on it. What is this letter called?
128475.e: The bill shows how much the visit to the doctor costs. The parents then check what the health insurance pays.
128475.m: A bill shows what something costs.

128476.q: What do you take to the doctor so they can see which health insurer you are with?
128476.e: Your insurance card shows your name and your health insurer. So the surgery knows where to send the bill.
128476.m: The insurance card belongs in every doctor's bag.

128477.q: Who does your insurance card belong to?
a: Only you, it has your name on it
128477.e: Every person has their own insurance card. You do not lend it to anyone.

128478.q: Roughly how big is the insurance card?
a: As big as a bank card
As big as an exercise book
128478.e: The insurance card is a small plastic card. It fits easily in a purse or wallet.
128478.m: Small as a bank card, important at the doctor's.

128479.q: Mia is healthy but still goes to the children's doctor. Why?
a: For a check-up to see if she is growing well
Because she has to hand in homework
Because it is the doctor's birthday
128479.e: Children go for check-ups regularly. The doctor measures height and weight and checks that everything is fine.
128479.m: A check-up means seeing if everything is fine.

128480.q: What does the doctor use to listen to your heart and lungs?
128480.e: The stethoscope has two earpieces and a round part that is placed on the chest. So the doctor can hear how the heart and lungs are working.
128480.m: With a stethoscope you can listen to the heart.

128481.q: What do you use to measure whether someone has a temperature?
128481.e: The thermometer shows the body temperature. If it is clearly higher than usual, you have a fever.

128482.q: What usually helps when a child has a fever?
128482.e: With a fever, the body needs rest and plenty of fluids. If it lasts a long time or is very high, you ask the doctor.
128482.m: With a fever: drink and rest.

128483.q: Where do you wait at the doctor's surgery until it is your turn?
128483.e: At the surgery you sit in the waiting room. You are called from there when the doctor has time.
128483.m: In the waiting room, be patient.

128484.q: What do parents usually do before taking you to the doctor?
128484.e: At most surgeries you phone beforehand and make an appointment. So the surgery knows when you are coming.
128484.m: First the appointment, then the doctor.

128485.q: Who often greets you at the reception of a doctor's surgery?
128485.e: The medical practice assistant welcomes you, takes your insurance card and helps the doctor.
128485.m: At reception, the practice assistant helps.

128486.q: Who checks whether your teeth are healthy?
128486.e: The dentist checks your teeth and looks for holes. You go for check-ups regularly.
128486.m: For healthy teeth: go to the dentist.

128487.q: Who often visits schools and shows how to brush your teeth properly?
128487.e: In many Swiss schools a dental care worker visits the classes. She shows how to brush teeth properly.
128487.m: You can learn to brush properly.

128488.q: How often a day should you brush your teeth?
128488.e: It is best to brush your teeth in the morning and in the evening. That keeps them healthy and fewer holes form.
128488.m: Morning and evening: brush your teeth.

128489.q: Roughly how long should you brush your teeth?
128489.e: Two minutes are enough to brush all your teeth well. An egg timer or a song helps you keep to the time.
128489.m: Two minutes for a bright smile.

128490.q: What damages teeth if you do not brush them?
a: Tooth decay, meaning holes in the teeth
128490.e: Tooth decay happens when sugar and bacteria stay on the teeth for a long time. Then the teeth get holes.
128490.m: Sugar plus no brushing means holes.

128491.q: When do you need a new toothbrush?
a: When the bristles are worn and bent
Only when it comes in a new colour
128491.e: When the bristles splay apart, the brush no longer cleans well. Then it is time for a new one, about every few months.

128492.q: Which morning snack is especially good for your teeth?
128492.e: Lots of sugar harms the teeth. Fruit, vegetables and water make a good snack.
128492.m: Water and an apple make teeth happy.

128493.q: How can you often recognise a pharmacy in Switzerland?
128493.e: Many pharmacies in Switzerland have a glowing green cross. So you can find them quickly.
128493.m: The green cross shows the pharmacy.

128494.q: Who works in the pharmacy and knows all about medicines?
128494.e: The pharmacist knows a lot about medicines. She explains how to take them properly.
128494.m: At the pharmacy, experts give advice on medicines.

128495.q: What does the doctor give you so that you can get a certain medicine at the pharmacy?
128495.e: For some medicines you need a prescription from the doctor. It says which medicine you need.
128495.m: Some medicines are only available with a prescription.

128496.q: What is the right thing to do with medicines?
a: Only take them when an adult gives them to you
128496.e: Medicines can help, but they can also harm. Children only take them when parents or the doctor give them.

128497.q: Where should medicines be kept at home?
a: High up, where small children cannot reach
On the floor in the children's bedroom
128497.e: Small children easily mistake tablets for sweets. That is why medicines belong in a safe place.
128497.m: Medicines: kept high up and safe.

128498.q: Lukas has a cough. The syrup tastes nice. May he take more than he was told?
a: No, only as much as the adults say
Yes, as much as he wants
128498.e: Even if a medicine tastes good, it is not a drink. Too much can be harmful.
128498.m: Even tasty syrup is a medicine.

128499.q: Where do you go if you are very ill and need to be cared for overnight?
128499.e: Many doctors and nurses work in a hospital. You can also stay overnight there until you are well again.
128499.m: In hospital you are cared for day and night.

128500.q: Who looks after the sick in hospital day and night?
128500.e: Nurses help the sick, give medicines and make sure they are all right.
128500.m: Nurses are always there in hospital.

128501.q: Leo has broken his arm. What does he often get so the bone heals well?
128501.e: A plaster cast keeps the broken bone still. So it can grow back together in a few weeks.
128501.m: The cast keeps the bone still.

128502.q: What can be used in hospital to look inside the body, for example at the bones?
128502.e: For an X-ray, a machine takes a special picture. It shows the bones.

128503.q: What is the place in a hospital called where you go with a sudden serious problem?
128503.e: Accident and emergency is open day and night. There people who need help straight away are treated.

128505.q: Which number do you call if there is a fire?
128505.e: 118 is the number for the fire brigade. For an ambulance you dial 144.
128505.m: If there is a fire, dial 118.

128506.q: What is the number for the police in Switzerland?
128506.e: You can reach the police on 117. The ambulance service is 144 and the fire brigade 118.

128507.q: Which emergency number also works in many other European countries?
128507.e: 112 is the European emergency number. It works in Switzerland too.

128508.q: What do you say first when you call 144?
a: Who you are and where you are
128508.e: The helpers need to know where to go. Say your name, the place and what has happened.
128508.m: Who, where, what: that is what you say in an emergency call.

128509.q: Is it all right to call 144 for fun?
a: No, the line must be free for real emergencies
Yes, but only at the weekend
128509.e: If someone calls for fun, the helpers have less time for people who really need help.

128510.q: After the emergency call, what do you do if the person on the phone still has questions?
128510.e: The person on the phone may need more information. They will also tell you what you can do. Only hang up when they say so.
128510.m: Only hang up when the helpers say so.

128511.q: How can you hear that an ambulance is on a call?
128511.e: On a call, the ambulance has flashing blue lights and a siren. Other cars then make way.
128511.m: Blue lights and siren: please make way.

128512.q: Who rides in the ambulance and helps the injured?
128512.e: Paramedics know how to help in an emergency. They treat the person and take them to hospital.

128513.q: What do cars do when an ambulance comes with blue lights flashing?
a: They drive faster in front of it
They stay in the middle of the road
128513.e: The ambulance has to get to the emergency quickly. That is why the other cars move to the side.

128514.q: What is the number for Rega, which helps with helicopters?
128514.e: Rega is the Swiss Air Rescue service. You can reach it on 1414, for example after an accident in the mountains.

128515.q: What does Rega often use to reach an accident in the mountains?
128515.e: No ambulance can get up into the mountains. The Rega helicopter can land there or winch the person up.
128515.m: Where no car can go, Rega flies.

128516.q: The Huber family is hiking in the mountains. The father falls and cannot walk any more. Who can they call?
128516.e: After an accident in the mountains, Rega is the right help. You call 1414.

128517.q: The little brother has drunk from a bottle of cleaning liquid. What does the mother do first?
a: She lets him play on his own
128517.e: At Tox Info Suisse on 145, experts say what to do. If the child is having trouble breathing or is unconscious, you call 144 straight away.

128518.q: What can be poisonous and should not be in children's hands?
128518.e: Cleaning products, medicines and some plants can be poisonous. They are kept safely put away.

128519.q: Can you simply eat mushrooms from the forest?
a: No, some mushrooms are very poisonous
128519.e: Many mushrooms look similar, but some are poisonous. In Switzerland you can have mushrooms checked at a mushroom inspection office.
128519.m: Never eat mushrooms you do not know.

128520.q: When should you always wash your hands?
a: Before eating and after using the toilet
128520.e: There are many germs on your hands that you cannot see. Washing your hands protects against illnesses.
128520.m: Before eating, after the toilet: wash your hands.

128521.q: Roughly how long should you soap and wash your hands?
128521.e: That is how long it takes to sing “Happy Birthday” twice. Then your hands are properly clean.
128521.m: Wash for as long as two birthday songs.

128522.q: Where should you sneeze or cough?
a: Into the crook of your elbow
128522.e: If you sneeze into the crook of your elbow, the germs spread less. Your hands stay cleaner.

128523.q: What do you do with a used tissue?
128523.e: Used tissues have germs in them. You throw them away and then wash your hands.

128524.q: Why is enough sleep important for children?
128524.e: The body recovers while you sleep. Children need lots of sleep to grow and to concentrate.
128524.m: A good night's sleep is half the learning.

128525.q: Roughly how many hours of sleep a night do schoolchildren up to age 9 need?
128525.e: School-age children need lots of sleep, usually between 9 and 12 hours. Adults need less.

128526.q: What helps you fall asleep well in the evening?
a: An exciting phone game in bed
128526.e: The light from screens keeps you awake. A calm story before bed helps more.

128527.q: Why is exercise good for you?
a: It makes your muscles and heart strong
It always makes you tired and ill
128527.e: People who move a lot strengthen their heart, muscles and bones. Exercise also puts you in a good mood.
128527.m: Exercise keeps you fit and cheerful.

128528.q: What is good exercise for children?
a: Playing on a tablet for a long time
128528.e: Children should be active every day. Playing outside is ideal for this.

128529.q: What protects your head when you are cycling?
128529.e: If you fall, the helmet protects your head. So fewer serious injuries happen.
128529.m: Helmet first, then onto the bike.

128530.e: A healthy plate is colourful. Vegetables and fruit give the body vitamins.
128530.m: The more colourful the plate, the better.

128531.q: What is the best drink when you are thirsty?
128531.e: Water quenches your thirst and has no sugar. In Switzerland you can usually drink tap water.

a: It helps the body protect itself against diseases
128532.e: A vaccination trains the body. So later it can fight a particular disease better.

a: The doctor or a trained professional
128533.e: Only a trained professional gives vaccinations, for example the children's doctor.

128534.q: Where is it written down which vaccinations you have already had?
128534.e: Your vaccination record lists every vaccination with the date. So your parents and the doctor know what is still missing.
128534.m: The vaccination record remembers every jab.

128535.q: Nina is scared of the vaccination. What can help her?
a: Breathing deeply and holding Mum's hand
Screwing up her eyes and wriggling
128535.e: A quick jab only hurts for a moment. Breathing calmly and holding on to someone helps many children.
128535.m: A small jab for big protection.

128536.q: What do we call the body's power to fight off illnesses?
128536.e: The body has its own defence system. Healthy eating, sleep and vaccinations make it stronger.
128536.m: Your immune defences are your body's police.

128537.q: Lara grazes her knee. What goes on the wound after cleaning it?
a: Sticky tape from a craft box
128537.e: A plaster protects the wound from dirt. So it can heal well.

128538.q: What do you do first with a small, dirty graze?
128538.e: First the dirt is rinsed out with water. Then a plaster goes on.

a: The help you give until professionals arrive
The first homework in the morning
The first game at break time
128539.e: First aid means helping straight away as well as you can. For example getting help or putting on a plaster.

128540.q: A child falls in the playground and is crying hard. What do you do first?
128540.e: Children help best by quickly fetching an adult. The adult then knows what to do.

128541.q: What belongs in a home first aid kit?
a: A ball and a skipping rope
128541.e: The home first aid kit has things for small injuries and illnesses. It is kept in a safe place.
128541.m: The first aid kit helps with small aches and pains.

128542.q: Mattia bumps his head and gets a lump. What often helps?
a: Blowing it with a hot hairdryer
128542.e: Cooling helps the lump swell less. You put something cold wrapped in a cloth on the spot.

128543.q: What do you do if you have slightly burnt your finger?
a: Blow on it hard and carry on cooking
128543.e: Cool, not ice-cold, water eases the pain. For large burns you get help straight away.

128544.q: What do you do when you have a nosebleed?
a: Lean your head slightly forward and pinch your nose
128544.e: Lean your head forward so no blood runs down your throat. Pinch the soft part of your nose for a few minutes.

128545.q: A bee stings Tim on the arm. What helps against the burning?
128545.e: Cooling eases the pain and swelling. If someone has trouble breathing, you call 144 straight away.
128545.m: A sting? Cool it and keep an eye on it.

128546.q: When do you go to the doctor?
a: When you are ill or have hurt yourself
When you want a new book
When you are learning to ride a bike
128546.e: The doctor examines you and knows what will help you get well.

128547.q: What does the doctor often ask first?
128547.e: The doctor wants to know what is wrong. So you tell her where it hurts and since when.

128548.q: Can the doctor tell everyone what is wrong with you?
a: No, she must keep it secret
128548.e: Doctors have a duty of confidentiality. What you tell them stays secret.
128548.m: At the doctor's, it stays between you.

128549.q: What is the doctor called that a family usually goes to first?
128549.e: The family doctor often has known the family for a long time. She helps with many illnesses or refers you to someone else.
128549.m: Go to the family doctor first.

128550.q: Who checks whether you can see well and might need glasses?
128550.e: The eye doctor tests your eyes. If you cannot see well, glasses can help.
128550.m: For your eyes: go to the eye doctor.

128551.q: What does health insurance pay for you, for example?
a: A visit to the doctor when you are ill
128551.e: Health insurance helps with costs to do with illness, for example the doctor or hospital. It does not pay for toys.
128551.m: Health insurance pays for health, not for toys.

128552.q: Why is it good that health insurance exists?
a: Nobody has to pay for expensive treatment alone
You never have to go to school again
128552.e: A stay in hospital can be very expensive. Thanks to health insurance, families do not have to pay all of it alone.

a: Getting enough sleep and playing outside a lot
128553.e: Sleep, exercise, good food and hygiene keep the body fit. So you get ill less often.
128553.m: Staying healthy is better than getting ill.

128554.q: Ben has a fever. What is better?
128554.e: Anyone with a fever needs rest. Also, this way you do not infect other children.

128555.q: How can you protect others from a cold?
a: Sneeze into your elbow and wash your hands
128555.e: Colds are passed on by germs. Washing your hands and sneezing properly help stop them spreading.

128556.q: Who can visit you in hospital if you have to stay overnight?
128556.e: In hospital your family is allowed to visit. With small children, parents can often even stay there.
128556.m: Even in hospital, your family is close.

128557.q: What is a hospital called that is only for children?
128557.e: In a children's hospital everyone specialises in children. There are also playrooms there.
128557.m: In a children's hospital, everything is about children.

128558.q: Which situation is a real emergency for 144?
a: Someone is lying on the ground and not responding
128558.e: If someone is unconscious or not responding, they need help at once. Then you call 144.
128558.m: If someone does not respond: call 144.

128559.q: What should you know by heart so you can help in an emergency?
a: The name of the neighbour's dog
128559.e: When you call for help, the helpers must know where to come. That is why it is good to know your own address.
128559.m: Know your address, it can help.

128560.q: Do you need money or credit on your phone to call 144?
a: Yes, you have to pay first
128560.e: In Switzerland you can call emergency numbers like 144, 117 and 118 for free.

128561.q: Do you still have to pay the health insurance premium if you were healthy all year?
a: Yes, you pay the premium anyway
128561.e: The premium is like a contribution to a shared fund. You always pay it, even if you stay healthy.
128561.m: You pay the premium even when you are healthy.

128562.q: Which of these is also insurance, like health insurance?
a: Insurance for your bike against theft
128562.e: There are many kinds of insurance, for example for the house, the car or the bike. Many people always pay in so that there is enough for everyone when damage happens.
128562.m: There is insurance for many things.

128563.q: After moving to Switzerland, how long do you have to take out basic insurance?
128563.e: Anyone who moves to Switzerland must get insured within 3 months. The insurance then applies backdated to the day they arrived.

128564.q: Within what time must parents insure their newborn baby with a health insurer?
a: Only when the child starts school
Within one week of the birth
128564.e: Babies need basic insurance too. If the child is registered within 3 months, it is insured backdated to the birth.

128565.q: Which statement about the benefits of basic insurance is true?
a: They are the same at all health insurers
Every health insurer offers completely different benefits
Expensive health insurers pay for many more treatments
Only big health insurers pay the doctor
128565.e: The law sets out what basic insurance pays for. That is why the benefits are the same at every health insurer, only the premiums differ.

128566.q: Who makes sure in Switzerland that health insurers follow the rules of basic insurance?
a: The Confederation, through the Federal Office of Public Health
128566.e: Health insurers are supervised by the Confederation, and the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) is responsible. It also checks the premiums, for example.
128566.m: The FOPH keeps a close eye on the health insurers.

128567.q: Can a health insurer make a profit from basic insurance?
a: No, it must not make a profit from it
Yes, as much as it likes
Only if all the insured are healthy
128567.e: Health insurers may not make a profit from basic insurance. They may only make a profit from supplementary insurance.

128568.q: How often do you normally pay the health insurance premium?
128568.e: The premium is a fixed amount, usually monthly. You pay it even if you stay healthy all year.
128568.m: The premium comes every month, ill or healthy.

128569.q: Luca never went to the doctor all year. Does he still have to pay the premium?
a: Yes, you always pay the premium
No, then the insurer pays him everything back
No, healthy people pay nothing at all
Only half, because he was healthy
128569.e: The premium is the price of being insured. You pay it so that you are covered if you get ill, even if nothing happens.
128569.m: Being insured costs money, even without a doctor's visit.

128570.q: What does the amount of the basic insurance premium NOT depend on?
128570.e: The premium depends on the health insurer, where you live, your age, the deductible and the model. Your health plays no part in basic insurance.

128571.q: Do men and women pay different premiums in basic insurance?
a: There are differences only in large cantons
128571.e: In basic insurance the premium does not depend on whether you are male or female. With the same insurer, the same place and the same age, everyone pays the same.
128571.m: Basic insurance: man or woman, same premium.

128572.q: Who normally pays the health insurance premium for an 11-year-old child?
a: The child with their pocket money
128572.e: Parents take out the insurance for children and pay the premium. Children's premiums are much lower than adults'.

128573.q: Why is the premium for children lower than for adults?
a: The law provides for lower premiums for children
Children are not allowed to see a doctor
128573.e: Lower premiums apply to children and young adults to ease the burden on families. But children get the same benefits.

128574.q: When do health insurers usually announce the new premiums for the next year?
a: In summer, at the start of July
128574.e: The new premiums are announced every autumn. After that there is time until the end of November to switch health insurer.
128574.m: Autumn: new premiums, time to compare.

128575.q: Where can you compare the premiums of all health insurers neutrally?
a: Only in a health insurer's adverts
128575.e: The Federal Office of Public Health runs an official premium calculator called Priminfo. There you can see the premiums of all insurers for where you live.
128575.m: Comparing is free: Priminfo from the Confederation.

128576.q: A pair of twins live in the same place, are the same age and have the same insurer and deductible. What is true of their premium?
128576.e: With the same insurer, place of residence, age, deductible and model, the premium in basic insurance is the same.

128577.q: On which date does the deductible start again from the beginning each year?
128577.e: The deductible applies per calendar year. On 1 January it starts again from zero, even if you had already reached it the year before.

128578.q: What usually happens to the premium if you choose a higher deductible?
a: The premium stays exactly the same
You no longer have to pay any premium
128578.e: Anyone who chooses a higher deductible pays more themselves when ill. In return the monthly premium is lower.

128579.q: Who is a high deductible more worthwhile for?
a: For people who rarely go to the doctor
For people who often need treatment
For everyone who likes going to the doctor
128579.e: People who rarely have doctor's costs save with the lower premium. People who are often ill quickly pay a lot themselves with a high deductible.
128579.m: Rarely ill: a high deductible can save money.

128580.q: Which of these deductibles can an adult choose in basic insurance?
128580.e: Adults choose a deductible between 300 and 2500 francs. 0 francs is only available for children.

128581.q: What is the highest deductible that adults can choose in basic insurance?
128581.e: The highest deductible adults can choose is 2500 francs. The lowest is 300 francs.

128582.q: Sara has a deductible of 300 francs. Her first doctor's bill of the year is 120 francs. Who pays?
128582.e: The bill is smaller than the deductible of 300 francs. So Sara pays all of it herself.
128582.m: Below the deductible, you pay yourself.

128583.q: When can you normally change the deductible in basic insurance?
a: At the start of a new year
128583.e: You can change the deductible from 1 January. If you want a lower deductible, you must tell the insurer by the end of November.
128583.m: Change your deductible: at New Year.

128584.q: What percentage of the costs do you normally pay as a co-payment in basic insurance?
128584.e: The normal co-payment is 10 % of the costs above the deductible. There is an upper limit per year.

128585.q: Tim is 12 and has a deductible of 0 francs. His doctor's bill is 200 francs. How much do his parents pay?
128585.e: With a deductible of 0 francs, only the 10 % co-payment applies. 10 % of 200 francs is 20 francs.

128586.q: Anna has a deductible of 300 francs. Her costs for the year are 1300 francs. How much does she pay herself?
128586.e: First she pays the 300 franc deductible. Of the remaining 1000 francs she pays a 10 % co-payment, which is 100 francs. Together that makes 400 francs.

128587.q: What is true of the co-payment for children?
a: Its yearly limit is lower than for adults
Children pay half of every bill
For children it has no upper limit
128587.e: Children also pay a 10 % co-payment. But each year it is limited to half the amount for adults, which is 350 francs.
128587.m: For children, the co-payment has a lower limit.

128588.q: What makes up cost sharing in basic insurance?
128588.e: Cost sharing is what you pay yourself towards your own treatment: the deductible and the co-payment. The premium does not count.

128589.q: Why do you have to share the costs even though you pay premiums?
a: So that people do not go to the doctor unnecessarily
Because otherwise the health insurer closes
Because otherwise you do not get a card
128589.e: People who pay part themselves think more carefully about whether a doctor's visit is needed. That helps keep health costs, and so premiums, lower.
128589.m: Paying a share makes people careful.

128590.q: What may a health insurer do with supplementary insurance that is forbidden with basic insurance?
128590.e: With supplementary insurance, the insurer may ask health questions and turn people down. In basic insurance it must accept everyone.
128590.m: Supplementary: the insurer may say no.

128591.q: What do parents often take out supplementary insurance for, for their child?
a: For the normal check-up at the family doctor
128591.e: Basic insurance usually does not pay for braces. That is why many parents take out dental supplementary insurance early.
128591.m: Braces? That is usually a matter for supplementary insurance.

128592.q: Does supplementary insurance have to be with the same health insurer as basic insurance?
a: No, it can be with a different insurer
Only children may have different insurers
Yes, otherwise the basic insurance lapses
128592.e: Basic insurance and supplementary insurance are separate. You can have them with different health insurers.
128592.m: Basic and supplementary can live apart.

128593.q: You would like a hospital room with fewer beds (semi-private). Which insurance do you need for that?
128593.e: Basic insurance pays for the general ward in hospital. For semi-private or private you need supplementary insurance.
128593.m: More comfort in hospital: supplementary insurance needed.

128594.q: Can you cancel supplementary insurance without losing basic insurance?
a: No, then you are no longer insured at all
128594.e: Supplementary insurance is a separate contract. If you cancel it, the basic insurance stays in place.

128595.q: Mia wants to take out her supplementary insurance with a new insurer. What should she do first?
a: Wait for the new acceptance, then cancel
128595.e: Because the new insurer may turn people down for supplementary insurance, you should get accepted first. Only after that do you cancel the old supplementary insurance.
128595.m: Switching supplementary: first acceptance, then cancellation.

128596.q: What is written on the insurance card, among other things?
a: Your name and your insurance number
128596.e: The card shows your name, date of birth, insurance number and health insurer. So the doctor or pharmacy can bill the costs.
128596.m: The card says who I am and where I am insured.

128597.q: Where do you typically show your insurance card?
a: At the pharmacy when collecting medicines
128597.e: With the card, the pharmacy bills the health insurer directly. You also need it at the doctor's surgery and in hospital.
128597.m: Pharmacy, doctor, hospital: show your card.

128598.q: What can you often find on the back of the Swiss insurance card?
128598.e: The back is usually the European Health Insurance Card. It helps with treatment in EU and EFTA countries.
128598.m: The back: a holiday helper for Europe.

128599.q: What should you do if you have lost your insurance card?
a: Tell the health insurer and order a new one
128599.e: If you lose it, you contact the health insurer. It sends a new card. You must never use someone else's card.

128600.q: In Switzerland, do you get help in an emergency even without an insurance card?
a: Yes, in an emergency you are always treated
No, no card means no help
Only with cash in your pocket
Only if your parents are with you
128600.e: In an emergency you are treated even if you do not have your card with you. The details can be provided later.
128600.m: An emergency comes before the card.

128601.q: Why is the premium usually lower in the family doctor model?
a: Because you partly give up the free choice of doctor
Because family doctors work for free
Because only children may choose this model
128601.e: The family doctor coordinates the treatment, which often saves costs. In return, you give up going straight to any specialist.

128602.q: Elias has the family doctor model and has bad stomach pains in the night. May he go straight to A&E?
a: No, never without the family doctor
Only with a letter from school
128602.e: In a real emergency you may always go straight to A&E. The rules of the model apply to normal treatment.

128603.q: What is the same in all models of basic insurance?
a: The phone number of the advice line
128603.e: Whether standard, family doctor or Telmed: basic insurance always pays the same benefits. Only the route to treatment and the premium change.

128604.q: What is the model called in which you can go straight to any doctor without restrictions?
a: Standard model with free choice of doctor
128604.e: In the standard model you have free choice of doctor. In return the premium is usually higher than in the other models.

128605.q: What can happen if, in the family doctor model, you go straight to a specialist without a reason?
a: The insurer may not pay for the treatment
The premium is halved at once
128605.e: If you do not follow the rules of the model, you risk the insurer not paying or having to switch to the standard model.
128605.m: It pays to follow the model's rules.

128606.q: Lea is 13 and breaks her arm while cycling. Which insurance pays?
a: The health insurance with accident cover
128606.e: Children are not insured against accidents through an employer. That is why health insurance also pays for their accidents.

128607.q: Jonas works 4 hours a week. He hurts himself playing football at the weekend. Who pays?
128607.e: Under 8 hours a week, you are only insured through your employer for accidents at work. Accidents in your free time are then paid by health insurance.
128607.m: Few hours: free-time accidents through health insurance.

128608.q: An apprentice works 40 hours a week at her training company. She falls while skiing on holiday. Who pays?
a: The accident insurance through the training company
Her parents entirely on their own
128608.e: Apprentices are employees. If they work at least 8 hours a week, they are also insured against accidents in their free time through the training company.
128608.m: Apprenticeship means: accidents through the company.

128609.q: Why can you sometimes exclude accident cover from your health insurance?
a: Because you are already insured against accidents through your employer
Because accidents are banned in Switzerland
Because the municipality pays for everything
128609.e: Anyone insured against accidents through their employer does not need accident cover from the health insurer. Excluding it lowers the premium.

128610.q: What counts as an accident for health insurers?
a: A sudden, unintended injury from outside
128610.e: An accident is a sudden event from outside that injures the body, for example a fall. An illness, on the other hand, develops inside the body.
128610.m: An accident comes suddenly from outside.

128611.q: Why does brushing your teeth well also pay off financially?
a: Because basic insurance usually does not pay for dental treatment
Because the toothbrush gives money back
Because then the premium is zero
128611.e: You usually pay for holes and fillings yourself. People who look after their teeth well need fewer expensive treatments.

128612.q: What do many municipalities or schools offer children?
128612.e: Many municipalities organise regular dental check-ups for schoolchildren. That way problems are spotted early.
128612.m: School dentist: check early, save later.

128613.q: Ali falls off his scooter and breaks a tooth. What usually applies?
a: As an accident, the accident cover pays for the tooth
Nobody ever pays for tooth accidents
The school has to pay for everything
128613.e: Damage to teeth caused by an accident is paid by accident insurance. For children, that is the accident cover of the health insurance.
128613.m: Tooth damaged in an accident: accident insurance.

128614.q: What applies in basic insurance to glasses for children?
a: The insurer pays a contribution towards them
The insurer pays for every pair of glasses in full
Children are not allowed to wear glasses
128614.e: For children and young people up to 18, basic insurance pays a contribution towards glasses or contact lenses if a doctor prescribes them.

128615.q: Does basic insurance pay for new lenses for healthy adults?
a: Yes, a new pair of glasses every year
128615.e: For adults, basic insurance only pays for glasses in the case of certain illnesses. Otherwise you need supplementary insurance or pay yourself.
128615.m: Glasses for adults: often a matter for supplementary insurance.

128616.q: What does a child usually need so that the insurer pays towards glasses?
128616.e: The health insurer pays its contribution if the glasses were prescribed by a doctor. That is why you have your eyes tested first.

128617.q: What should you do when a doctor's bill arrives at home?
a: Check the bill and keep it
Throw it away unread at once
128617.e: You check whether the treatment is correct and keep the bill. Depending on the system, you pay it and then send it to the insurer.
128617.m: Read, check and keep the bill.

128618.q: What does a refund from the health insurer mean?
a: The insurer pays you back money for a bill you have paid
You give the insurer money as a present
You get your premium back every year
128618.e: If you have paid a bill yourself, you send it to the insurer. It pays you back its share, minus the deductible and co-payment.

128619.q: How can you submit a doctor's bill to many health insurers today?
a: Only in person at head office
Only by fax on a Sunday
Not at all, it is forbidden
128619.e: Many health insurers offer an app that lets you photograph and send the bill. Post works too.
128619.m: Submitting a bill: app or postbox.

128620.q: What does it mean when the pharmacy bills the health insurer directly?
a: The insurer pays the pharmacy, and you pay your share later
You never have to pay anything
The pharmacy gives you the medicines for free
The bill goes to your school
128620.e: The insurer pays the pharmacy directly. Afterwards it sends you a statement for your share, meaning the deductible and co-payment.
128620.m: Billed directly does not mean free.

128621.q: What can you do if a doctor's bill lists a treatment you did not have?
a: Ask the surgery or the insurer
128621.e: Bills can contain mistakes. You ask the doctor's surgery or the health insurer. That also helps save costs.

128622.q: What is a benefits statement from the health insurer?
a: An overview of what the insurer paid and what you pay
128622.e: The benefits statement shows the bill amounts, the insurer's share and your own share of the deductible and co-payment.

128623.q: Why is it worth sending doctor's bills to the insurer even when they are below the deductible?
a: So the insurer counts them towards the deductible
Because otherwise the insurer forbids them
So the premium falls at once
128623.e: The insurer adds the bills together. That way it knows when the deductible has been reached and it starts to pay.
128623.m: Submit all bills, even small ones.

128624.q: Who is responsible for premium reductions?
a: The canton you live in, together with the Confederation
128624.e: The cantons pay out premium reductions, and the Confederation contributes money. The rules differ from canton to canton.
128624.m: Premium reductions: a matter for the canton.

128625.q: The Rossi family has little money and three children. What could help them with health insurance premiums?
a: Applying to the canton for a premium reduction
128625.e: Families on a low income can get a premium reduction. In some cantons you have to apply for it, in others it comes automatically.
128625.m: Do not cancel, get help instead.

128626.q: Which statement about premium reductions is true?
a: The rules differ from canton to canton
They are the same amount in every canton
You only get them after an accident
128626.e: Each canton decides for itself who gets how much of a premium reduction. That is why it is worth asking your own canton.

128628.q: Why do many people switch health insurer for their basic insurance?
a: To get a new house number
128628.e: The benefits of basic insurance are the same everywhere. But switching can often save on the premium.

128629.q: What is the safest way to send your cancellation to the health insurer?
a: By text message to a friend
By word of mouth at the bus stop
Not at all, the insurer notices by itself
128629.e: With a registered letter you can prove that the cancellation arrived in time.

128630.q: What is sensible before cancelling your basic insurance?
128630.e: Switching is only worthwhile if the new insurer is cheaper. So you first compare the premiums for where you live.

128631.q: If you switch basic insurance, what happens to the supplementary insurance at the old insurer?
a: It stays in place unless you cancel it
128631.e: Basic and supplementary insurance are separate contracts. The supplementary insurance stays as long as you do not cancel it yourself.

128632.q: After switching basic insurance, what must you show when you have treatment?
a: The card of the new insurer
The card of the old insurer
128632.e: From the switch onwards, the new insurer is responsible. So you show the new insurance card at the doctor's and the pharmacy.

128633.q: What does solidarity mean in health insurance?
a: Healthy people help pay for the care of the sick with their premiums
Everyone pays only their own costs
128633.e: Everyone pays premiums into a shared pot. From it, the costs of people who are ill at the moment are paid.
128633.m: Everyone pays in, and whoever is ill gets help.

128634.q: Why does health insurance only work if many people take part?
a: Because the costs are spread across many people
Because doctors only treat large groups
Because otherwise the insurer does not print cards
Because you never get ill on your own
128634.e: The more people pay premiums, the better the high costs of individual sick people can be covered. That is the idea of insurance.
128634.m: Many together carry what one alone cannot.

128635.q: Which example shows solidarity in basic insurance?
a: Young, healthy people pay the same as people who are often ill
Healthy people get everything back at the end
Every person has their own insurer
128635.e: In basic insurance you pay regardless of your health. So healthy people help carry the costs of the sick.
128635.m: Same premium for all, however healthy.

128636.q: Why is basic insurance compulsory for everyone?
a: So that everyone is insured and the costs are shared
So that health insurers get rich
So that nobody goes to the doctor any more
So that children get more homework
128636.e: If insurance were voluntary, perhaps only sick people would join. With compulsory insurance, everyone is protected and the costs are spread.

128637.q: When does basic insurance normally pay for a medicine?
a: When it is prescribed by a doctor and on the insurer's list
Always, even sweets from the shop
Only when it is especially expensive
Only when you buy it abroad
128637.e: Basic insurance pays for medicines that a doctor prescribes and that are on an official list. You pay for many over-the-counter products yourself.
128637.m: Prescribed and listed: then the insurer pays.

128638.q: When does basic insurance pay for physiotherapy after an injury?
a: When a doctor has prescribed it
128638.e: Physiotherapy is paid for by basic insurance if it is prescribed by a doctor. The deductible and co-payment still apply.

128639.q: Leonie is on holiday in Italy and gets ill. What helps her at the doctor's there?
128639.e: The European Health Insurance Card on the back of the insurance card helps with necessary treatment in the EU and EFTA.
128639.m: In Europe: turn your card over.

128640.q: Why do families often take out travel or supplementary insurance for trips far away?
a: Because basic insurance pays only up to a limit abroad
Because you never get ill abroad
Because otherwise the plane will not take off
128640.e: Abroad, basic insurance only pays for emergencies up to a certain limit. In countries with high medical costs that can be too little.

128641.q: Which number do you dial in Switzerland for an ambulance?
128641.e: 144 is the emergency number for the ambulance service. 117 is the police, 118 the fire brigade and 1414 Rega.

128642.q: Which hospital ward does basic insurance pay for?
128642.e: Basic insurance pays for a stay on the general ward. The medical treatment there is just as good.
128642.m: General ward: good medicine for everyone.

128643.q: Which statement about recommended vaccinations for children is true?
a: Basic insurance pays for many recommended vaccinations
Only supplementary insurance pays for vaccinations
The school pays for vaccinations in full
128643.e: Basic insurance pays for many vaccinations recommended by the Confederation, for example for children. Prevention can avoid later costs.
128643.m: Prevention is part of it too.

128644.q: What can everyone do so that premiums rise less sharply?
a: Only go to the doctor when it is necessary
Buy as many medicines as possible
Go to hospital with every sniffle
128644.e: Premiums depend on health costs. Anyone who is careful about treatment and checks bills helps keep costs low.

128645.q: Where can you get neutral advice if you are in a dispute with your health insurer?
a: At the health insurance ombudsman's office
128645.e: The health insurance ombudsman's office helps free of charge and neutrally with problems between insured people and insurers.
128645.m: Dispute with your insurer? Ask the ombudsman.

128646.q: What can happen if you do not pay the premium?
a: You get reminders and debt collection may follow
You are automatically no longer insured
The insurer lets you off the premium
128646.e: Basic insurance stays compulsory, even with unpaid premiums. The insurer sends reminders and can claim the money through debt collection.

128647.q: What applies to the premium for young adults aged 19 to 25?
a: Many insurers have a lower premium
They pay no premium at all
They pay the highest premium of all
They are not allowed to be insured
128647.e: For young adults up to 25, insurers offer lower premiums than for older adults. The children's premium applies up to 18.
128647.m: Up to 25: usually a bit cheaper.

128648.q: Paul only sends his cancellation of basic insurance on 15 December. What happens?
a: He stays with the old insurer for another year
He switches at New Year anyway
He is not insured at all from January
The insurer must release him at once
128648.e: To switch on 1 January, the cancellation must arrive by the end of November. If it arrives too late, you stay with the old insurer for another year.
128648.m: Cancelling too late means waiting a year.

128649.q: What do you mainly need for the first step in the Telmed model when you have symptoms?
128649.e: Telmed stands for telemedicine. The first step is a call to the medical advice line, which then recommends what to do next.
128649.m: Telmed starts with a phone call.

128650.q: What do you often have to fill in when applying for supplementary insurance?
128650.e: For supplementary insurance, the insurer asks about your health. Then it decides whether and on what terms it will accept you.
128650.m: Supplementary: the insurer asks about your health.

128651.q: In the family doctor model, who sends you to a specialist, for example a skin doctor?
128651.e: In the family doctor model, the family doctor writes a referral when a specialist is needed. That keeps the treatment coordinated.
128651.m: The family doctor decides who helps next.

128652.q: What is the difference between the premium and the deductible?
a: You always pay the premium, the deductible only when there are costs
They are exactly the same thing
You pay the deductible every month, the premium never
Only the insurer pays the premium to you
128652.e: The premium is the fixed amount you pay regularly. You only pay the deductible when you really have treatment costs.
128652.m: Premium always, deductible only with costs.

128653.q: Marco has a deductible of 300 francs. His costs for the year are 500 francs. How much does he pay himself?
128653.e: He pays the 300 franc deductible. Of the remaining 200 francs, a 10 % co-payment is added, which is 20 francs. Together that makes 320 francs.
128653.m: First the deductible, then 10 % of the rest.

a: An accident during a football match on Sunday
128654.e: An occupational accident happens at work. The employer's accident insurance is always responsible for it.

128655.q: If the doctor's surgery bills the health insurer directly, what are you entitled to as a patient?
128655.e: Even if the surgery bills the insurer directly, it must give you a copy of the bill. That way you can check it.
128655.m: You are allowed to see every bill.

128656.q: How is a premium reduction usually paid out?
a: Directly to the health insurer, so the premium gets lower
Not at all, it is only a promise
128656.e: The canton usually pays the premium reduction directly to the health insurer. The insured people then get a lower premium bill.
128656.m: The reduction goes straight to the insurer.

128657.q: Why do young people in basic insurance help pay for the costs of older people?
a: Because everyone pays into the same pot
Because young people never have medical costs
Because older people pay no premium
Because the insurer punishes young people
128657.e: Older people often need more treatment. Because adults of all ages pay similar premiums, young people help out. Later they benefit from it themselves.
128657.m: Today I help, later I will be helped.

128774.q: What must you not throw into the toilet?
128774.e: Wet wipes do not dissolve in water. They block the pipes. They belong in the bin.
128774.m: Only toilet paper goes into the toilet.

128775.q: Where do you take empty batteries?
a: To the battery collection in the shop
128775.e: Batteries contain substances that harm nature. Many shops have a collection box for them.
128775.m: Empty batteries belong in the collection box.

128776.q: The yoghurt is one day past its “best before” date. What do you do?
a: Look at it, smell it and taste it carefully
Throw it away unopened at once
128776.e: “Best before” means it is definitely fine until then. It is often still good to eat afterwards. Check it with your eyes, nose and tongue.
128776.m: Look, smell and taste instead of throwing away.

128777.q: How do you carry a knife safely through the kitchen?
128777.e: If the point faces down, you cannot hurt anyone by accident. Walk slowly while you do it.
128777.m: Always keep the knife point facing down.

128778.q: Which of these is a vegetable?
128778.e: Broccoli is a green vegetable. Apple, cherry and pear are fruits.
128778.m: Broccoli is a vegetable, the apple is a fruit.

128779.q: Your old toy is still good, but you would like something new. What is kind to the environment?
128779.e: When you swap, you have something new to play with, and nothing is thrown away. This way fewer new things are needed.
128779.m: Swapping is better than throwing away.

128780.q: What do you do when you leave a room and nobody else is in it?
128780.e: A light in an empty room uses electricity for nothing. With one click of the switch, you help save energy.
128780.m: When you go out, switch the light off.

128781.q: What do you use to wash dishes clean by hand?
128781.e: Warm water and washing-up liquid loosen grease and food leftovers. Then you rinse the dishes and let them dry.
128781.m: Warm water and washing-up liquid get things clean.

128782.q: Where do your dirty socks belong?
128782.e: In the laundry basket you collect dirty clothes until they are washed. This keeps your room tidy.
128782.m: Dirty laundry goes in the laundry basket.

128783.q: Which animal does the milk you usually buy in the shop come from?
128783.e: Most milk in Switzerland comes from cows. Butter, cheese and yoghurt are also made from milk.
128783.m: Milk usually comes from the cow.

a: Cares for sick people in hospital
128784.e: Polymechanics drill, mill and turn metal parts. They often work with computer-controlled machines.
128784.m: Polymechanics make parts out of metal.

128785.q: What does a healthcare assistant do?
a: Cares for and looks after people in hospital or a care home
128785.e: A healthcare assistant helps sick and elderly people, for example by measuring temperature and blood pressure, and helps with washing and eating.
128785.m: The healthcare assistant looks after people.

a: Furniture and windows out of wood
128786.e: Joiners saw, plane and glue wood. This is how tables, cupboards, doors and windows are made.

128787.q: What does an electrician do in a new house?
a: Lays electric cables and fits sockets
128787.e: Electricians make sure the lights work in a house and that electricity comes out of the sockets. They work very carefully because electricity is dangerous.
128787.m: The electrician brings electricity into the house.

128788.q: Where does a social care worker often work?
a: In a nursery with small children
128788.e: A social care worker plays, does crafts and eats with children at the nursery. Some also look after elderly people or people with disabilities.
128788.m: Social care workers work in nurseries.

a: Plants and looks after flowers, trees and lawns
128789.e: Gardeners work outside with plants. They lay out gardens, cut hedges and mow lawns.

128790.q: What does a retail specialist do in a shop?
a: Advises customers and fills the shelves
128790.e: Retail specialists advise customers, work at the till and make sure the goods are neat and tidy on the shelves.
128790.m: In a shop, retail specialists help you.

128791.q: Where does a cook usually work?
a: In an office full of files
128791.e: Cooks prepare vegetables, fry meat and arrange the food nicely on plates. They work in restaurants, hospitals or canteens.
128791.m: The cook cooks in a restaurant.

129075.q: What does a farmer do on the farm?
a: Looks after animals and grows plants
Drives a train across the country
129075.e: Farmers look after cows, pigs or chickens and grow grain, potatoes or vegetables.
129075.m: A lot of our food comes from farms.

129076.q: Which vehicle does a farmer often need in the field?
129076.e: With the tractor the farmer pulls trailers, a plough or a mower. This makes work in the fields much easier.
129076.m: The tractor is the favourite vehicle on the farm.

129077.q: Which material does a joiner work with most?
129077.e: Joiners make furniture such as tables, cupboards or beds out of wood. They also make doors and kitchens.
129077.m: The joiner turns wood into furniture.

129078.q: Who needs a plane to make wood smooth?
129078.e: With the plane, the joiner takes thin shavings off the wood. This makes the wood nice and smooth and straight.

129079.q: Which tools does a hairdresser need every day?
a: A brush and a paint roller
129079.e: The hairdresser cuts hair with scissors and a comb. She often needs a hairdryer too.
129079.m: Scissors and a comb belong in a hair salon.

129080.e: A hair salon has mirrors, chairs and washbasins. That is where hairdressers wash, cut and style hair.
129080.m: The hairdresser works in a salon.

129081.q: What does a train driver do?
129081.e: The train driver sits at the front in the driver's cab and brings the train safely and on time to its destination.
129081.m: The train driver drives the train.

129082.q: Where does the train driver sit during the journey?
a: Right at the front in the driver's cab
On the roof of the train
In the last carriage with the suitcases
129082.e: The driver's cab is at the front of the train. From there the driver can see the tracks and the signals.
129082.m: The train driver sits at the front of the train.

129083.q: What does a nurse do in hospital?
129083.e: Nurses take temperatures, give medicines and help patients in everyday life.
129083.m: Nurses help sick people get well.

129085.q: Where does a polymechanic usually work?
129085.e: In the workshop there are big machines for working metal. That is where the polymechanic works.

129086.q: What does a cook do in a restaurant?
129086.e: The cook chops, fries and cooks in the restaurant kitchen. Then the food is served to the guests.
129086.m: The cook cooks for lots of guests.

129087.q: Why do cooks often wear a white hat?
a: So that no hair falls into the food
So that they don't get cold
So that you can see them from far away
So that the sun doesn't dazzle them
129087.e: The tall white chef's hat keeps the hair together. That way no hair falls into the food.
129087.m: The chef's hat protects food from hair.

129089.q: Why should only experts work on cables and sockets?
a: Electricity can give you a serious shock
129089.e: An electric shock can seriously injure people. That is why only trained electricians work on cables and sockets.

129091.q: Which tool does a gardener use to give plants water?
129091.e: Plants get water from the watering can or the hose. Without water they would wilt.
129091.m: Plants need water from the watering can.

129092.q: Who helps when your dog is ill?
129092.e: The vet examines and treats sick animals. She also vaccinates dogs and cats.
129092.m: Sick animals go to the vet.

129093.q: Mia is taking her cat to be vaccinated. Where does she go?
129093.e: At the vet's surgery, animals are examined, vaccinated and treated.

129094.q: What is one of the jobs of police officers?
a: They keep people safe and maintain order
They bake bread for the village
They plant trees in the forest
129094.e: The police help at accidents, direct traffic and make sure everyone sticks to the rules.

129095.q: What does the fire brigade do besides putting out fires?
a: It also helps with accidents and floods
129095.e: The fire brigade rescues people and animals and helps with accidents, floods and storm damage.
129095.m: The fire brigade helps in many emergencies.

129096.e: Pilots fly planes or helicopters and bring passengers safely to their destination.
129096.m: The pilot flies high in the sky.

129097.q: What is the place where the pilot sits in the plane called?
129097.e: The cockpit is right at the front of the plane. It has lots of buttons, screens and the controls.
129097.m: The plane is flown from the cockpit.

129098.e: Postmen and postwomen deliver the post to people's letterboxes.

129100.q: What does a teacher do at school?
129100.e: Teachers explain reading, writing, maths and much more. They help children learn.

129101.q: What does the teacher often write on in the classroom?
129101.e: On the board or a big screen, the teacher shows what the class is learning.
129101.m: The board is the class's big exercise book.

129102.q: What does an IT specialist mainly work with?
129102.e: IT specialists write programs, set up computers and help when something doesn't work.
129102.m: The IT specialist speaks the language of computers.

129103.q: Who writes the programs for games and apps?
129103.e: Every game and every app is a program. IT specialists write the commands for the computer.
129103.m: Behind every app there is a program.

a: Walls out of bricks and concrete
129104.e: On the building site, bricklayers build walls out of bricks and concrete.
129104.m: The bricklayer builds brick by brick.

129105.q: Which tool does a bricklayer need for the mortar?
129105.e: With the trowel, the bricklayer spreads mortar between the bricks. That way they hold together firmly.

129106.q: Where does a bricklayer usually work?
129106.e: New houses go up on building sites. Bricklayers work there together with many other tradespeople.
129106.m: On the building site, a house grows.

129107.q: Why do people on a building site wear a helmet?
129107.e: Things can fall down on a building site. The helmet protects the head from injuries.

129108.q: Why does a baker often get up very early?
a: So that the bread is fresh in the morning
Because the bakery is closed in the evening
Because dough only rises at night
129108.e: Many people want fresh bread for breakfast. That is why bakers often start in the middle of the night or early in the morning.
129108.m: Getting up early brings fresh bread.

129109.q: Where is the bread baked in a bakery?
129109.e: In the hot oven, dough turns into crusty bread.
129109.m: The oven makes the bread crusty.

129111.q: Where do you pay for your shopping in a shop?
129111.e: At the till the goods are scanned, and you pay with cash or a card.

129112.q: What does a carpenter build out of wood?
129112.e: Carpenters build large wooden structures, for example the frame of a roof or whole wooden houses.
129112.m: The carpenter builds the roof out of wood.

129113.q: What is the difference between a joiner and a carpenter?
a: The carpenter builds large wooden structures, the joiner makes furniture
The joiner only works with metal
There is no difference at all
129113.e: Both work with wood. The carpenter builds roofs and wooden houses, the joiner makes furniture, doors and kitchens.

129114.q: Who do you call when water is dripping from the pipe?
129114.e: Plumbers lay water pipes and fit washbasins, toilets and showers.
129114.m: If it drips, the plumber helps.

129115.q: Who needs a pipe wrench for work?
129115.e: With the pipe wrench, the plumber tightens or loosens pipes and nuts.

129116.q: What does a painter do on a building site?
129116.e: Painters paint walls, outside walls, windows and doors. This makes a house look nice and protects it.
129116.m: The painter brings colour into the house.

129117.q: Which tool does a painter need for big walls?
129117.e: With a paint roller, the painter can paint large areas quickly and evenly.

129118.q: What does a mechanic do in the garage?
129118.e: In the garage the mechanic changes tyres and oil, for example, and repairs whatever is broken on the car.
129118.m: In the garage, the car gets fit again.

129119.q: Which tool does a mechanic often need?
129119.e: With a spanner, the mechanic tightens or loosens screws and nuts.

129120.e: Foresters look after the forest. They decide which trees are cut down and where new ones are planted.
129120.m: The forester looks after the forest.

129121.q: Who cuts down trees in the forest with a chainsaw?
129121.e: Forestry workers work in the forest. They cut down trees, plant young trees and look after forest paths.
129121.m: Foresters and forestry workers work in the forest.

129122.e: At the dentist your teeth are checked. If a tooth has a hole, the dentist fixes it with a filling.
129122.m: The dentist keeps your teeth healthy.

129123.q: Why do schoolchildren go for regular dental check-ups?
a: So that holes are found early
So that you never have to brush again
129123.e: At a check-up, small holes are spotted early. Then fixing them is easier and hurts less.

a: Hands out medicines and gives advice on them
129124.e: You get medicines at the chemist. The pharmacist explains how to take them properly.
129124.m: At the chemist you get advice and medicine.

129125.q: What does a bus driver do?
129125.e: Bus drivers follow a timetable from stop to stop and take people where they want to go.
129125.m: The bus driver takes you to the stop.

129126.q: How does the bus driver know when to be where?
129126.e: The timetable shows when the bus leaves from each stop. The driver sticks to it.
129126.m: The timetable tells you when the bus comes.

a: A place where small children are looked after
129128.e: Kita is short for Kindertagesstätte, a day nursery. Children are looked after there while their parents work.
129128.m: A Kita is a day nursery.

129129.e: Butchers, today called meat specialists, prepare meat and also make sausages from it.

129130.q: What does a dressmaker, officially a clothing designer, do?
129130.e: Clothing designers sew clothes and alter them, for example when a pair of trousers is too long.
129130.m: Clothes are made with a needle and thread.

129131.q: Who needs a sewing machine for work?
129131.e: With a sewing machine you can sew fabric much faster than by hand.

129132.q: Leo has a flat tyre on his bike. Who can help him?
129132.e: Bike mechanics, officially bicycle mechanics, fix tyres, brakes and chains.

129133.e: Florists work in a flower shop. They make bouquets and flower decorations for celebrations.
129133.m: The florist works magic with flowers.

129134.q: Who steers a ship on the lake?
129134.e: Passenger boats run on Swiss lakes. At the front, the captain steers the boat.
129134.m: On a ship, the captain is at the wheel.

129135.q: What does a zookeeper do at the zoo?
a: Feeds the animals and cleans the enclosures
Sells ice cream at the entrance
129135.e: Zookeepers make sure the zoo animals are well. They feed, clean and watch the animals.
129135.m: At the zoo, the zookeeper looks after the animals.

129136.q: Who comes in the ambulance when someone is injured?
129136.e: Paramedics give first aid and take injured people to hospital. Their number is 144.
